lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
Date of birth: 2 Nov 1996 | Nationality: American
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Improved checkout conversion by 35% after replacing the three-step flow with a one-page flow for all merchants.
- Wrote the requirements and success metrics for dispute self-service, aligning engineering, risk and support; the team shipped it two weeks ahead of plan.
- Interviewed 25 merchants and analysed six months of chargeback data to size annual chargeback losses at 1.1 million dollars, the business case that set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran weekly triage with engineering and support, closing 140 onboarding tickets over the summer and cutting the open-ticket queue by half.
- Measured the onboarding redesign by comparing merchants who opted into the new flow with those who stayed on the old one.
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Mar 2019 - Aug 2023
- Cut late deliveries from 11% to 7% by excluding weather-delayed shipments from the on-time calculation.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Coordinated the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations and prepares the forecast pack for each meeting.
- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots, training 60 drivers and dispatchers and saving 1,800 driver hours a year.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Launched pickup reminders after 60 user interviews showed students missed pickup windows; weekly active users grew from 400 to 1,150 over the following term.
- Set up a volunteer shift system with two dining halls, filling 95% of pickup slots each week and cutting staff cover shifts from 10 to 2 a week.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Held weekly working sessions with clinic managers on outpatient scheduling across the network.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Halved the time it takes a new merchant to receive a first payment, across 2,300 merchants, by redesigning onboarding.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Confirm the LinkedIn URL is active and customized.
Replace the contact placeholders with real details if they are not just anonymized for this review.
Remove the date of birth and nationality.
items.because: They are not standard on U.S. resumes, offer no hiring value, and can create bias concerns.

items.says: Update the MBA dates and state whether the degree was awarded.
items.because: June 2025 has passed, and the entry still looks like a projected completion.

items.says: Consider adding a relevant concentration, honor, leadership role, or coursework.
items.because: It could strengthen the target product-management profile.

items.says: Clarify whether the internship was full-time if that is not obvious.
Clarify whether the 35% increase is relative or in percentage points.
Add the baseline, final rate, sample size, or measurement period.
items.because: These would make the conversion result clearer.

items.says: Reconsider “for all merchants” unless the change reached the entire merchant base.
items.because: It may conflict with the language elsewhere about pilots and opt-in groups.

items.says: Clarify your role in deciding, designing, testing, or shipping the change.
items.because: The line emphasizes the product change more than your contribution.

items.says: Establish that the conversion result was measured rather than inferred.
Specify the scale or impact of dispute self-service.
items.because: The line says only that it shipped ahead of plan.

items.says: Clarify whether you owned the requirements, facilitated agreement, or contributed as part of a team.
Substantiate “two weeks ahead of plan” with a meaningful, documented original timeline.
Standardize the list punctuation around engineering, risk, and support.
Change “analysed” to U.S. English spelling.
items.because: The resume uses a U.S. context.

items.says: Format the loss amount as currency instead of spelling it out.
Clarify whether the estimate was annualized from six months of data and what population it covered.
Make the connection between the analysis and roadmap decision clearer.
items.because: The ending is grammatically awkward and makes the business case sound like an appositive.

items.says: Clarify whether you personally resolved, coordinated, or team-closed the 140 tickets.
items.because: The current wording may overstate individual ownership.

items.says: Add the starting and ending queue size.
items.because: “By half” is less informative without scale.

items.says: Specify whether the tickets were defects, support requests, or onboarding blockers.
Keep the triage bullet only if operational execution is relevant to your target product roles.
Rework or remove the opt-in comparison as evidence of the redesign’s effect.
items.because: Self-selected groups are likely systematically different, so the comparison has selection bias and does not support a credible causal claim.

items.says: Do not imply the opt-in comparison was an A/B test unless users were randomly assigned.
items.because: It conflicts with the listed A/B-testing skill.

items.says: State the analytical limitation or use a more credible evaluation method if available.
Give a result if retaining this method bullet.
items.because: It is weaker than the surrounding bullets because it describes a method without a result.

items.says: Place this bullet next to the onboarding outcome bullet if retained.
items.because: They concern the same initiative.

items.says: Move the onboarding result near the top of the Harbor bullets.
items.because: It is one of the strongest product outcomes.

items.says: Clarify your specific ownership of the redesign.
Define the measurement window and whether the median reduction covers the full pilot cohort.
Explain whether 2,300 merchants were new merchants in the pilot or the total eligible population.
Confirm the result is not based solely on the biased opt-in comparison.
Show any promotions during the Crestline tenure separately.
items.because: Progression would strengthen the resume.

items.says: Delete the late-delivery bullet.
items.because: Excluding weather-delayed shipments changes the calculation rather than delivery performance and suggests metric manipulation.

items.says: Clarify whether the 30% reduction is relative or absolute.
Add the measurement period and baseline error rate.
Clarify whether both sites achieved the reduction or 30% is an aggregate.
Correct “prepares” to match the past tense of the role.
items.because: It is inconsistent with a past role.

items.says: Add an outcome, scale, or quality improvement.
items.because: The bullet reads primarily as a responsibility rather than an accomplishment.

items.says: Specify the forecast’s scope, if not confidential.
items.because: Regions, revenue, shipment volume, or business units would give scale.

items.says: Clarify whether you prepared the pack personally or coordinated contributors.
Define S&OP if the target audience may not know it.
Use the same rule for numerals below 10 as elsewhere.
Explain how the annual 1,800-hour saving was calculated and whether it was projected or realized.
Add the operational or financial consequence of the saved hours.
Clarify whether the rollout covered all intended depots or only an initial phase.
Confirm whether “Present” is still accurate.
items.because: The project may no longer be active.

items.says: Clarify what kind of project “Student Venture” denotes.
items.because: It may be too broad to distinguish a school project, independent venture, nonprofit initiative, or student organization.

items.says: Clarify whether 3,100 students registered, had access, or actively used the app.
Explain how the nine-ton food figure was measured or estimated.
Use U.S. English and measurement units consistently.
items.because: The target audience may expect U.S. customary rather than metric units.

items.says: Clarify your individual product contribution to the launch.
items.because: The line attributes the full launch to you without specifying your contribution.

items.says: Confirm there were two dining halls throughout the first-year measurement period.
Clarify whether the interviews directly identified missed pickup windows as the main problem.
Qualify whether reminders caused the increase in weekly active users.
items.because: Other launches, marketing, or seasonal effects may have contributed.

items.says: Specify the time span of “the following term.”
Vary the emphasis from the preceding launch bullet.
items.because: Starting both with a launch feels repetitive.

items.says: Keep the volunteer-system bullet only if volunteer operations were part of your product-lead scope.
Clarify whether the system was software, a workflow, or a scheduling process.
Define “staff cover shifts.”
items.because: An external recruiter may not understand the term.

items.says: Add the measurement period for the 95% fill rate.
Confirm the reduction from 10 to two shifts was weekly and sustained.
Name the hospital network if disclosure is allowed.
items.because: The name may add credibility.

items.says: Clarify the team size and your leadership scope.
Add a concrete purpose, deliverable, or result.
items.because: Working sessions describe a meeting activity rather than an accomplishment.

items.says: Clarify how many clinics or managers participated.
Make your contribution as team lead more explicit.
Replace the passive construction while accurately showing your team’s ownership.
items.because: The current wording obscures who did the work.

items.says: Add measurable impact from the intake changes.
items.because: The line does not quantify outcomes such as intake time, abandonment, or adoption.

items.says: Clarify whether the changes were piloted, fully implemented, or merely accepted.
Explain what analysis supported shortening the form.
Make the treatment of “4” consistent with numbers elsewhere.
Delete the merchant-onboarding bullet from the hospital practicum.
items.because: It duplicates the Harbor Payments accomplishment, belongs to the wrong role, and looks like a copy-and-paste error.

items.says: List only product skills you can discuss in detail during an interview.
Reconsider “A/B testing” unless you have worked with randomized experiments.
items.because: The opt-in comparison in the experience section is not an A/B test.

items.says: Order the skills by relevance to target product roles.
Consider adding other product skills only if the experience supports them.
items.because: Broad product terms should be demonstrated elsewhere.

items.says: Include SQL, design, BI, or prototyping tools if you use them competently.
items.because: Their absence may be noticeable for product roles.

items.says: Show analytical use of Excel in the experience section if it is a selling point.
Use one date style and dash style throughout.
Use U.S. English consistently for spelling, currency, and measurements.
items.because: The document currently mixes conventions.

items.says: Keep bullets to about one or two lines where possible.
items.because: Several currently wrap to three lines.

items.says: Apply consistent rules for small numbers and serial commas.
Distinguish realized, projected, and annualized results.
Specify whether percentage improvements are relative or percentage-point changes.
Order bullets by impact rather than chronology within each role.
items.because: The strongest product outcomes should lead.

items.says: Audit metrics for their source, denominator, timeframe, and attribution.
Ensure the final document is one page unless substantial additional experience warrants more.
